sovereign_country.strategic_role: 拉美西语近岸软件研发外包与数字客服中心

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Global App Store Optimization and Multilingual Organic Search

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Colombia (single unitary national jurisdiction; no separate sub-state company register for SAS formation)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law with Common Law elements in commercial arbitration and company law practice
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Colombia-United States Trade Promotion Agreement (in force 2012)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Ley 1258 de 2008 (SAS regime); Código de Comercio (Decreto 410 de 1971); Ley 526 de 1999 (UIAF); Ley 1121 de 2006 (LA/FT financing); Ley 2013 de 2019 (PEP transparency); Decreto 830 de 2021 and Resolución UIAF 164 de 2021 (Beneficiario Final / UBO register); Circular Externa 100-000003 de 2019 and Circular Externa 2021-03 de la Superintendencia de Sociedades (SAGRILAFT).

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized articles of incorporation (Acta de Constitución by private document) with exhaustive UBO annex
Original notarized power of attorney for each non-resident shareholder/UBO executing the incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the shareholder's country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille OR Consular Legalization (non-Hague states)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of UBO passport and official residence proof (translated by certified translator into Spanish)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Issuing government authority of the beneficial owner

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of good standing / excerpt of the corporate register for any corporate shareholder of the SAS
Judicial background certificate (Certificado de Antecedentes Judiciales) of the legal representative and compliance officer
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Domestic notarial certification (no apostille required for domestic documents)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory risk-based screening of UBOs, legal representatives, and commercial counterparties against OFAC SDN, UN Security Council consolidated list, EU/HM Treasury sanctions, and Colombian national lists (UIAF Listas Nacionales, Policía Nacional records); PEP verification against public officials under Ley 2013 de 2019; enhanced due diligence if any matched record; real-time automated sanctions screening at onboarding and continuous periodic re-screening; audit trail retained for at least 10 years.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Único Empresarial y Social (RUES) - www.rues.org.co, operated by Confecámaras and the competent local Cámara de Comercio (e.g., Cámara de Comercio de Bogotá)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Corporate name must be composed of Spanish-language terms; generic foreign expressions and global trademarks may be included only as supplementary 'sigla' or secondary designation; the denominación must be clearly distinguishable from existing registered names; no non-Roman scripts allowed; all names must be transcribed in Latin script accent-compliant form.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Fondo de Inversión, Fondo de Pensiones, Fiduciaria, Valores, Bolsa
Policía, Ejército, Defensa Civil, Cruz Roja
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon name rejection by the Cámara de Comercio, the applicant must file a written 'derecho de petición' within 10 business days before the same Chamber invoking the homonimia search results; if the rejection is reiterated, appeal to the Superintendencia de Sociedades (tax/administrative procedures division) must be submitted through the SIREM administrative channel within the remaining 5 business days; alternatively, the applicant may immediately request a fresh homonimia certificate with a modified name and proceed with registration.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permitted for a low-risk digital services agency (ISIC 7310) provided the registered address is a real, physical location in Colombia (coworking/business-center box address acceptable) capable of receiving official communications and accessible for inspection; the address must be stated in the articles of incorporation and reported to DIAN (RUT); fully virtual/no-desk domicile is legally possible but creates an elevated risk of recharacterization as a 'domicilio ficticio' by tax and corporate authorities.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low-to-moderate; approximately 15% unannounced physical inspection probability within the first three years for a standard low-risk SAS; the probability increases if periodic tax filings, payroll, or invoice evidence reflect inconsistencies with the declared operating address.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Homonimia / name clearance certificate (certificado de homonimia)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory Chamber tariff schedule (allows national tariff)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Drafting and notarization of the private articles of incorporation (Acta de Constitución) including UBO annex
Registration fee in the Mercantile Registry (registro mercantil) with certification of existence for the SAS
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Tariff set by Decree 1074 de 2015 and Supersociedades resolution based on registered capital

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Legal opinion on UBO piercing, AML/SAGRILAFT design, and statutory license assessment (ISIC 7310 no license needed)
Hague apostilles of foreign shareholder documents and certified Spanish translations
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Cancillería / Apostille-competent authority in origin country
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Per-document apostille fee and certified translator market rate

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: SAGRILAFT manual and AML/KYC onboarding toolkit (including PEP and OFAC screening protocol)
Pre-RUT processing before DIAN and electronic signature certificate (Certicámara)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: DIAN pre-registration is free; PKI certificate statutory rate

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Law 1258 of 2008 (Sociedad por Acciones Simplificada), Articles 1-20; supplementary Commercial Code (Código de Comercio), Book II, Title I, and Decree 1074 of 2015
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Cámara de Comercio del domicilio principal (e.g., Cámara de Comercio de Bogotá)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Documento Privado de Constitución de Sociedad por Acciones Simplificada (Private Incorporation Deed under Law 1258 of 2008)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum authorized capital; each subscribed share must be paid at least 25% of its nominal value at incorporation, in cash or in kind, with the balance payable according to the bylaws, generally within 24 months. No escrow account requirement applies.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: The execution of the incorporation instrument, subscription of all shares, and initial payment of the subscribed capital under the bylaws are ratified. RESOLVED: The registered office shall be the address stated in the constitutive deed, domiciled in Colombia. RESOLVED: [Name A], [Name B], and [Name C] are appointed as legal representative/president, vice president/secretary, and statutory auditor, respectively, each with the powers and obligations set under Law 1258 of 2008. RESOLVED: The legal representative is instructed to complete the Chamber of Commerce registration, apply for the RUT, and perfect all remaining acts for full corporate existence.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cámara de Comercio virtual (Registro Único Empresarial - SIIC)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit up to three proposed corporate names through the online platform of the Chamber of Commerce of the registered office. The system checks for identity or similarity with existing registered names. Once approved, the name is reserved for a non-renewable period of 30 calendar days. Pay the corresponding reservation fee online.
required_dossiers: Valid identity document of the requesting founder
Completed online name request form
Proof of payment of the name reservation fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected or queried for similarity, immediately submit the alternative names provided in the reservation request. If the objection cannot be overcome, withdraw the request and file a new application with a distinctly differentiated name.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of the private incorporation deed and bylaws
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notaría de elección de los fundadores or Cámara de Comercio where shareholder signatures are authenticated
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Lawyers prepare the estatutos (bylaws) containing corporate name, registered office, corporate purpose, authorized and subscribed capital, share classes and payment terms, administration structure, and legal representative powers. Each founder, or their attorney-in-fact, executes the private incorporation document. Signatures must be authenticated before a notary or at the Chamber of Commerce if real property is contributed, the deed must be granted in a public deed.
required_dossiers: Draft bylaws and incorporation instrument
Valid identity document or passport of each shareholder
Bank or notarial evidence of the minimum 25% capital payment in cash
Independent valuation report if contributions are made in kind
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the document is formally deficient or signatures are not properly authenticated, correct the defect and re-execute the instrument. In the case of capital payment disputes, provide supplementary evidence of deposit or valuation and refile.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration with the Chamber of Commerce and payment of statutory fees
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cámara de Comercio of the registered office — Registry of Commerce
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the executed incorporation document and required ancillary forms via the Chamber's online portal or at the office window. Pay the incorporation registration tariff and stamp taxes. Submit the sworn declaration of final beneficiaries and the pre-RUT information form used by DIAN. The system reviews the legal requisites and registers the company in the Mercantile Registry.
required_dossiers: Executed private incorporation deed
Pre-RUT (Registro Único Tributario) information form
Sworn declaration of final beneficiaries (Declaración de Beneficiarios Finales)
Proof of payment of registration fees and stamp taxes
Valid identity document of the legal representative
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the submission is incomplete or rejected, the Chamber will issue a judicial notice with specific corrections needed. Address each point in writing, resubmit the corrected document, and pay any additional fee, if applicable. A formal reconsideration request may be filed if the rejection is meritless.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Issuance of the certificate of existence and legal representation
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Once the registration is complete, obtain the Certificado de Existencia y Representación Legal (Certificate of Existence and Legal Representation). This certificate evidences the legal incorporation of the SAS, names the legal representative, and confirms the registered office. The NIT (Número de Identificación Tributaria) is generated and must be validated in the DIAN system..
required_dossiers: Registered incorporation deed number or electronic proof of registration
Payment of registry tariff
Government-issued identity document of the legal representative
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the certificate is delayed, request written confirmation of registration status from the Chamber. If the certificate contains errors, apply for a correction or annotation explaining the data discrepancy. Recovery of prior data may require a petition under the Chamber's administrative review procedures.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: DIAN (Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales) and municipal treasury of the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: With the Certificate of Existence in hand, finalize the RUT by updating or completing the DIAN registration, including industrial and commercial tax (ICA) enrollment where applicable. Register the bank accounts that will receive capital contributions and file the accounting books. Obtain the municipal zoning certificate (uso del suelo) and, if required, the fire safety inspection approval for the physical office.
required_dossiers: Certificado de Existencia y Representación Legal
Legal representative's identity document
Lease contract or proof of ownership of the registered office
Bank certificate of the corporate account
Zoning certificate (Certificado de Uso del Suelo)
Fire safety certificate (Certificado de Bomberos) for the office premises, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the DIAN queries the RUT application, provide the requested clarifications or appoint a legal representative through consultation laws. For municipal issues, correct the zoning conflicts by rehearsing the permitted use with the local planning authority. Any refusal must be appealed through the corresponding administrative remedies.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: No industrial licensing authority applies because the activity is a non-industrial service (ISIC 7310 advertising and app growth services). For physical office matters, the competent local authority is the municipal planning office and the fire department (Cuerpo de Bomberos).
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: None required for the service business; the relevant regulatory prerequisite is the municipal zoning certificate (Certificado de Uso del Suelo) and registration with the industrial and commercial tax (ICA).

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Autoridad Nacional de Licencias Ambientales (ANLA) for projects of national or sectorial significance; otherwise Corporación Autónoma Regional (CAR) for regional jurisdiction
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — the proposed activity is a knowledge-based service with no fixed pollution source, no discharge of hazardous waste, and no environmental impact mitigation intervention required under Decree 2041 of 2014 or applicable regional environmental plans
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: The operation must comply with municipal solid waste segregation rules, wastewater discharge thresholds under Resolución 631 of 2015 for washrooms and coffee areas, and indoor air quality guidelines under Resolution 610 of 2010; no emissions at industrial production level are expected.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification from the official fire department (Cuerpo de Bomberos) confirming emergency exits, extinguishers, and evacuation signage; structural load inspection verified through the leasehold's existing building safety certificate; and workplace compliance under Resolution 312 of 2019 requiring an occupational health and safety management system (SG- SST) with risk assessments and employee training records.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales (DIAN) — National Tax and Customs Administration of Colombia. Digital taxpayer portal: 'Sede Electrónica DIAN' at www.dian.gov.co; transactional e-services are operated on the MUISCA platform. Foreign-owned entities interact through a Colombian resident legal representative ('apoderado') recorded in the Registro Único Tributario (RUT).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: 1. Incorporate the S.A.S. under Law 1258 of 2008, filing the private incorporation document with the local Cámara de Comercio (Chamber of Commerce); no minimum paid-in capital is required and the Chamber registration produces corporate existence. 2. Apply online at the DIAN Sede Electrónica for the Registro Único Tributario (RUT); the RUT generates the definitive NIT (Número de Identificación Tributaria) — the sole statutory tax identification number for income tax, VAT, and withholding purposes. 3. Obtain a DIAN-habilitated electronic signature certificate ('firma electrónica') and bind it to the entity's MUISCA e-tax account. 4. Complete the 'Habilitación de Factura Electrónica' (e-invoicing authorization) and, in the same RUT file, declare VAT responsibility ('responsable de IVA'), municipal ICA tax registration, and withholding-agent status; update the RUT to include the export activity (ISIC 7310) before issuing any zero-rated export invoice. 5. File the annual beneficial-ownership ('beneficiario final') report with the Chamber of Commerce and appoint a Colombian resident 'revisor fiscal' only if statutory thresholds are exceeded; for a low-asset S.A.S., statutory audit/revisor requirements may not apply.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation; Territorial_Scope: Worldwide for resident S.A.S.; Pass_Through_Eligible: Not available (no check-the-box or partnership flow-through election); Tax_Exempt_Zone: Not applicable (ordinary national regime; a 20% Zona Franca rate requires separate DIAN Free-Zone authorization). Concretely, the S.A.S. is a Colombian taxpayer resident under ET art. 12-1 and is taxed on worldwide net income at the general corporate rate of 35% for fiscal years 2024-2025; the same entity is the IVA taxpayer for services rendered; non-resident shareholders are not themselves taxed at entity level but dividends distributed abroad are subject to separate Colombian dividend withholding rules.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Colombia has no US-style check-the-box election. Statutory elections relevant to this S.A.S. include: (i) the 'Régimen Simple de Tributación – SIMPLE' (Law 1943 of 2018, as amended), an elective consolidated income-VAT-ICA regime for entities with annual gross income not exceeding 85,000 UVT (approx. COP 4,233 million for FY2025; 2025 UVT = COP 49,799), with combined progressive rates of 0%–14.5% and simplified e-filing; (ii) election to enter an established Zona Franca or obtain 'Usuario Industrial de Bienes y Servicios' status, giving a 20% corporate income tax rate and certain VAT exclusions (not assumed here); (iii) election to claim input VAT refunds on a periodic basis instead of offsetting them against future VAT liability; and (iv) transfer-pricing documentation elections under OECD-aligned Colombian rules. Anti-hybrid and Colombian CFC provisions apply, so hybrid-branch/check-the-box mechanisms are unavailable; an S.A.S. always remains a corporation for tax purposes.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banco de la República de Colombia, acting through the Ministry of Finance and Public Credit and the Superintendencia Financiera de Colombia as executing regulators for the Colombian foreign exchange regime (Régimen Cambiario).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Colombian Peso (COP) is fully convertible for current account transactions but subject to mandatory channeling through authorized foreign exchange intermediaries. Capital account transactions, including foreign direct investment and outbound profit remittances, require prior registration with Banco de la República and are generally free of quantitative restrictions, provided that tax obligations and annual corporate filings are current. Dividend remittances are permitted after statutory financial statements adoption and tax payment, but the corresponding central bank registration and withholding payment proof must be presented to the local commercial bank. No general prior approval is required for routine service export collections, yet all proceeds must enter the national exchange market in compliance with channeling rules.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Exporters, including digital service providers generating foreign-currency revenue from SEO and localization projects for a Colombian S.A.S., must channel all export collections through the domestic foreign exchange market via an authorized local commercial bank within a maximum term of 13 months from the date of the invoice or the service provided. The mandatory conversion ratio is 100% of the foreign-currency proceeds, unless the Banco de la República has expressly authorized the exporter to hold foreign-currency bank accounts abroad or indefinitely offshore funds. The sale to the local market must occur within 5 business days of collection if the money is received directly into a foreign account, or immediately if credited to a local USD settlement account. Compliance is evidenced through the monthly foreign-exchange declaration (Formulario No. 14) submitted to the Central Bank by the commercial bank.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Moderate. Wise B2B and Payoneer are not authorized deposit-taking banking institutions in Colombia; they cannot issue a Colombian NIT or provide a local account for mandatory FX channeling, nor can they act as managers for the Banco de la República foreign-exchange registration. Their lawful use is as auxiliary collection and disbursement rails for low-value cross-border payments, provided that the underlying services are not part of Colombian export proceeds requiring surrender to the official exchange market. For an SEO localization agency receiving global performance-based fees, WISE/Payoneer balances must be swept in-country on a monthly basis to an authorized commercial bank account and reported in the FX declarations. As a primary treasury account, these EMIs are deemed non-compliant with Colombian capital controls and a local bancarized account is mandatory.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote onboarding is possible for low-risk S.A.S. entities, but in practice a Colombian resident legal representative, attorney-in-fact, or director must attend an initial videoconference KYC interview; most tier-1 banks require one physical appearance at a head office in Bogotá or Medellín to sign the account mandate and validate physical corporate documentation. The S.A.S. foreign shareholders may be absent, but they must execute a notarized power of attorney presented through the bank's International Desk, containing the foreign shareholder's passport, proof of address, and apostilled incorporation certificates. Digital signature via the Firma Electrónica (electronic signature) and Certificado Digital is accepted by Bancolombia and Davivienda, but physical presence is waived only after the legal representative initiates a face-to-face protocol at the designated main branch.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Single-member foreign-owned S.A.S. with no physical office, no local employees, and no Colombian revenue.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide a notarized lease agreement in Bogotá, the individual tax ID (RUT) of a Colombian resident general manager, six months of banking statements from a foreign parent, detailed global commercial contracts with APAC/LatAm clients, and a sworn statement that the entity will engage local bilingual personnel for ASO and localization work.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-throughput cross-border payments flowing from payment aggregators (Wise/Payoneer) without identifiable underlying invoices.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Submit a fully reconciled transaction ledger matching each inbound payment to a signed client purchase order or localization invoice, the corresponding SWIFT/payment settlement statements, and a record of the monthly Formulario No. 14 FX declaration filed through the designated commercial bank, together with a signed AML representation letter certifying that all counterparties are free from OFAC and EU restrictive measures.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Rapid creation of corporate structure followed by high foreign capital injection with a shareholder located in a high-risk jurisdiction.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Deliver a comprehensive beneficial ownership chart (Régimen de Propiedad Beneficiaria) certified by the Colombian notary, a bank reference letter from the foreign source bank issued within 30 days, a tax affidavit of the parent company clarifying its commercial activity, and an independent economic substance report prepared by a local auditor confirming the S.A.S. has sufficient operational capacity to execute the SEO market strategy.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: All inbound capital injections for the Colombian S.A.S. must be routed via SWIFT MT103 (or MT202 for large interbank transfers) with the correspondent bank and the local commercial bank as final beneficiary, using the official Banco de la República foreign-exchange purpose concept 3618 (invexes from the parent company) or concept 2005 (capital contributions). The sender must include the NIT (tax ID) of the Colombian S.A.S., the concept word 'INVESTMENT - REGISTRO INVERSIONES INTERNACIONALES', and the reference to the foreign investment registration number issued by Banco de la República. The receiving bank will assign an exchange declaration form (Formulario No. 14) for the transaction, which must be closed before any COP disbursement. For subscription of shares by a non-resident, the paid-in capital is initially not subject to FX surrender, but the equivalent COP proceeds disbursed from the USD account must be tracked and registered as an investment against the account statement.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Trade settlements for supplier disbursements (e.g., outsourcing of localization, ASO development, linguistic quality assurance) must be executed through the authorized local bank via SWIFT MT103 under the official 'Outbound Services' purpose code corresponding to the nature of the service (e.g., 4730 – technical services, 4740 – marketing/advertising services). Commercial letters of credit (LC) are permissible but generally unnecessary and administratively expensive for intangible service contracts; open account MT103 with 30/60/90 days terms is the standard clearing rail. All outbound payments require an approved binding contract, proof of prior month-end FX declaration, and the appointed bank's validation that the payment qualifies under the risk management rules. For disbursements to the final shareholders as profit dividends, the bank requires a payment order accompanied by the Fiscal Certificate of Dividend Declaration, evidence of tax withholding, and the registered foreign investment certificate.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable forward contracts (DFCs) in COP/USD offered by the local authorized bank for commercial hedging of dollar receivables and payables

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) in COP/USD conducted with offshore counterparties for hedging non-export cash flows only, provided the initial exposure is properly documented and the NDF settlement is made in USD

Cross-currency interest rate swaps (CCIRS) for long-term financing structures used to swap COP-denominated liabilities into USD obligations, subject to bank regulatory approval and Banco de la República registration
FX options (European style) on COP/USD executed through the local authorized entity for premium-based hedging, limited to commercial real exposures and not permitted for speculative trading

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual renewal of the Mercantile Registration (Renovación de la Matrícula Mercantil)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cámara de Comercio of the jurisdiction of the registered domicile, acting through the RUES (Registro Único Empresarial y Social)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually from 1 January through 31 March for all entities registered in the commercial registry as of 31 December of the preceding year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late renewal triggers a Chamber surcharge under the applicable tariff; continued non-renewal may subject the entity to Superintendencia de Industria y Comercio sanctions and eventual removal from the mercantile registry, loss of good-standing certification, and inability to obtain standing certificates or perform routine corporate filings.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Deposit of approved annual financial statements and annexes
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cámara de Comercio of the company's registered address / RUES
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Financial statements for the fiscal year ended 31 December must be prepared and submitted for shareholder approval no later than 31 March of the following year; the approved financial statements must be deposited with the Chamber of Commerce within one month of approval, generally no later than 30 April.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to deposit can result in fines imposed by the Superintendencia de Sociedades or the relevant Chamber authority, negative annotations on commercial standing, and enforcement of the statutory obligation through administrative inspection and possible loss of limited-liability protection in commercial evidentiary matters.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax return (Declaración de Renta y Complementarios)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: DIAN – Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually for the preceding tax year during DIAN's assigned filing window, historically running from early April to late June, allocated by the last two digits of the NIT tax identification number.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing incurs a fine of up to 5% of the total tax payable, with default interest; the DIAN may issue an assessment based on substitute information, impose additional penalties under the Estatuto Tributario, and initiate administrative enforcement against company assets.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: DIAN – Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales, electronic filing system
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually within DIAN's published filing window, generally May through July following the fiscal year, with due dates assigned by the final digits of the NIT.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-submission, late submission, or incomplete data triggers sanctions under Article 651 of the Estatuto Tributario, including fines up to 10,000 UVT and reduction penalties for corrected information; continued non-compliance can cause RUT suspension and increased tax inspection risk.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: An S.A.S. must appoint a Revisor Fiscal and obtain a statutory audit opinion when total gross assets or gross income exceed the equivalent of 3,000 current monthly legal minimum wages (SMMLV) as of the applicable fiscal year-end; the Revisor Fiscal is also compulsory when required by law, by sector-specific regulation, or by the shareholders' agreement. Below the threshold, no independent statutory audit is mandatory, but shareholders may voluntarily designate an auditor or revisor fiscal.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS/NIIF as adopted in Colombia under Law 1314 of 2009, organized by Decreto Único Reglamentario 2420 of 2015 and additional regulatory decrees: full IFRS for large and publicly accountable entities, IFRS for SMEs for intermediate entities, and NIF Micro for eligible micro businesses.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Beneficial-ownership data is confirmed annually through the mercantile renewal and through the DIAN exogenous information return; any transfer of shares is effective only after inscription in the statutory shareholder register, and the company must record the transfer in the same calendar year in which it occurs. Changes in the ultimate beneficial owner, particularly a natural person holding 5% or more, directly or indirectly, trigger an update of the corporate data presented to DIAN and the Chamber in the next renewal cycle. Share transfers in an S.A.S. do not require notarial form; inscription in the shareholder ledger is the controlling perfection act.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Shareholders (Libro de Registro de Accionistas)
Minutes Book of Shareholders' Meetings (Libro de Actas de Asamblea General)
Attendance Register of Shareholders' Meetings (Libro de Asistencia a Asambleas)
Minutes Book of the Board of Directors, where a board is constituted (Libro de Actas de Junta Directiva)
Share Transfer and Capital Movement Ledger
Statutory Accounting Books (Diario and Mayor or integrated system)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 150–900 per year for a virtual office or registered-address service in Bogotá or Medellín; the annual Chamber renewal tariff for a small S.A.S. is typically USD 30–180 in addition, depending on assets and turnover.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 4,000–18,000 for a full Revisor Fiscal or certified public audit of a small to mid-size digital agency; a limited financial review or assurance engagement may range from USD 1,200–3,500.

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No general tax holiday for digital or software agencies. Preferential incentives are limited to: (a) qualifying Research, Technological Development and Innovation (STI) investments eligible for a 25% non-refundable tax credit; (b) certain investments in newly developed critical micro-regions (ZOMAC) that may obtain a graduated income tax exemption for up to 9 years; and (c) special deductions for donations to cultural and scientific entities. A typical ASO/SEO localization agency operating in Bogotá will ordinarily face the standard 35% corporate rate.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Formulario 110 – Declaración de Renta y Complementarios para Personas Jurídicas y Asimiladas; filed electronically through DIAN's MUISCA platform at www.dian.gov.co.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual (with mandatory quarterly prepayments made through the same DIAN portal under the 承租 tax instalment regime).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Generally due in the 4th to 9th month following the fiscal year-end, depending on taxpayer classification and the last digit of the NIT, as published annually in a DIAN deadline resolution. Calendar-year entities face a filing season that runs from April to September of the following year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 01 – NIT, name, and ISIC activity code
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxpayer identification, legal corporate name, and the primary ISIC v4 economic activity code (in this case 7310).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The foreign shareholders are not listed as filers; the Colombian SAS submits the declaration under its own NIT as a local entity. TIN and NIT must match DIAN registration precisely.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductible payments made to foreign related parties: subcontracting, licensing, royalties, services, fees, and interest paid abroad.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Deductibility is conditioned on withholding at the statutory rate for remittances abroad and, where applicable, on submitted transfer pricing documentation. Payments without source withholding or with mismatched economic substance will be disallowed or recharacterized as hidden dividends.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 80 – Taxable net income (renta líquida gravable)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Income after allowable deductions, exemptions, and transfer pricing adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Computed at the SAS level; non-resident shareholders have no direct filing obligation in this line. The taxable base must include transfer-pricing arm’s-length adjustments and exclude any passive dividend income already subject to corporate tax.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 88 – Income tax payable (impuesto a cargo)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Result of applying the 35% corporate income tax to the taxable net income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The payment is made by the Colombian entity. Non-resident shareholders do not sign or file this line; their exposure is through dividend withholding at the distribution stage.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Aggregate summary of withholding taxes withheld and remitted to DIAN during the fiscal year, including dividends paid to non-residents, royalties, interest, and other cross-border payments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The SAS acts as statutory withholding agent. For each dividend remittance to non-residents, the 5% dividend withholding tax must have been withheld and paid using Form 350 on a monthly basis; this line merely reconciles those payments.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalties under ETArticle 641: an extemporaneous filing surcharge ranging from 5% to 20% of tax due, or if no tax due, up to 1% of gross income. Late payment triggers monthly interest at the DIAN official rate (approximately 1.5% per month) plus a late payment surcharge of up to 100% of the unpaid tax in cases of gross negligence. Failing to file altogether can lead to administrative fines up to 20% of the assessed tax and criminal prosecution for aggravated evasion when the amount evaded exceeds legal criminal thresholds.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 5% statutory withholding tax for dividends distributed to non-resident shareholders from earnings already subject to Colombian corporate income tax. Where dividends are paid out of exempt or otherwise untaxed profits, the withholding rate is 35% (the corporate headline rate) at the time of distribution.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim reduced or exempt rates under a Double Tax Agreement (DTA), the non-resident beneficial owner must: (1) furnish a valid Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) issued by the foreign tax administration; (2) provide a declaration of beneficial ownership and absence of abusive conduit arrangements; (3) submit the TRC and supporting forms to the Colombian payer or directly to DIAN before the payment date; and (4) where reduced withholding was initially applied, support the position in the local Form 350 withholding tax return. Alternatively, any excess withholding may be reclaimed through a DIAN refund process within statutory deadlines. The treaty-reduced dividend WHT for most Colombian DTAs is 0%–10% depending on the treaty and ownership threshold.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory withholding: interest owed to non-residents is generally 15%; royalties and technical/administrative service fees paid abroad are generally 15% as well. DTA relief typically reduces royalty WHT to 10%–15% and interest WHT to 0%–15%, subject to limitation-on-benefits and mutual agreement provisions. Late or omitted WHT creates same-day deposit obligations and heavy penalties.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Mandatory transfer pricing documentation (Local File) is required for corporate taxpayers that have related-party transactions and whose gross income exceeds approximately 61,000 UVT (approx. COP 3.1 billion / USD 700,000) or whose total related-party transaction value exceeds approximately 10,000 UVT (approx. COP 500 million). A Master File and Country-by-Country Report are required only for multinational groups with consolidated group revenue above COP 100 billion. Questions about compliance threshold: even when documentation is optional, an annual Transfer Pricing Information Return (Form 120) must sometimes be filed where any of the income, asset, or transaction filters are met.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Colombia does not adopt a standalone 'Economic Substance Regulations' regime as found in some offshore centers. However, Colombian tax law and DIAN administrative doctrine apply the substance-over-form principle to challenge artificial structures and shell companies: the entity must demonstrate actual premises, personnel, administrative capacity, and decision-making in Colombia. A SAS with no local substance but only a registered PO Box risks having its payments to non-residents recharacterized as dividends or royalties subject to higher WHT, CFC attribution under controlled-foreign-company rules, and denial of treaty benefits for lack of beneficial ownership or permanent establishment exposure.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Willfully understating revenue, inflating deductible expenses, or hiding cross-border payments in an ASO/SEO agency’s books to reduce the Colombian corporate income tax base.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative fine under DIAN can reach up to 160% of the evaded tax, plus moratory interest at the official rate. Criminal prosecution under Colombian Criminal Code Article 434 for tax evasion is punishable by imprisonment of 36 to 108 months (approximately 3 to 9 years) and a fine equivalent to the evaded tax amount.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and legal representatives can be personally bound for the unpaid corporate tax where they signed fraudulent returns or participated in the concealment; criminal judges may impose civil restitution, disqualification from managing companies, travel bans pending proceedings, and custodial imprisonment for the directors actually charged.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Money laundering and unexplained asset growth
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the SAS to channel untaxed overseas advertising revenue through shell foreign accounts, mixing ill-gotten funds with licit client receipts, or processing online payments in a way that deliberately obscures the source and beneficial ownership.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Colombian Criminal Code Article 323, money laundering carries a prison sentence of 10 to 30 years and fines of up to 1,000 times the current statutory minimum wage (SMMLV). Funds and assets connected to the offence may be confiscated.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Personal criminal liability falls on any director, shareholder, or compliance officer who knowingly participates in laying or disguising illicit proceeds. Convictions lead to immediate prison terms, travel bans, bank account freezes, and civil liability for all laundering losses suffered by third parties.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Entering into related-party transactions with foreign app-store optimization affiliates, trademark-holding companies, or knowledge-process outsourcing providers without preparing a Local File, submitting Form 120, or applying arm’s-length pricing for intra-group royalties and marketing fees.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: DIAN may disallow expenses for lack of documentation, levy fines of up to 1% of the value of unreported related-party transactions per infraction, and charge interest on any adjusted tax underpayment. Understating the tax base substantively can trigger the same evasion sanctions as classic tax evasion.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Signing false compliance certificates or knowingly filing incomplete transfer-pricing documentation exposes the CFO and legal representative to civil damages and to criminal liability for fraud against the tax administration if the underpayment exceeds criminal thresholds; can include prohibition from serving as directors and personal seizure of assets.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Failure to withhold and remit cross-border dividend and royalty WHT
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Distributing dividends to foreign shareholders or paying royalties and interest abroad without applying the statutory withholding rates, or using DTA relief without a valid TRC and beneficial-ownership file.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: DIAN imposes on the withholding agent a sanction equal to 100% of the tax not withheld, plus moratory interest and late-payment surcharge. Additionally, recurring failures may be treated as criminal nonpayment of withholding tax, generating imprisonment for the responsible officer.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The managing director and accountant who execute an unauthorized tax-free remittance become personally liable for the withholding shortfall; criminal cases can bring preventive detention, travel bans, disgorgement of economic benefit, and direct civil reparation to the tax authority.
